path: Page body sections. Each renders the page's own content rather than replacing it, keeps its calls to action as real links or buttons, and composes at most three cores from earlier waves. These are public page idioms rather than re-implementations of any particular work, so they are originated and carry no credits except where one follows a published accessibility pattern. Nothing fetches from the network, nothing adds a dependency, and every default already looks finished on the dark ground and the light one.

components.title: Feature Grid
components.brief:
A page body section that places the page's own heading and introduction before a generated list of features from JSON, [{ glyph, heading, copy }]. Each feature is an article inside a semantic list. The glyph is text, marked aria-hidden, and the heading and copy carry the meaning without it. The default frame shows six complete features in a three column grid, with short glyphs such as [#], {+}, and <*>. Every cell contains a glyph, heading, and one line of copy, so no bordered area holds bare ground. At narrow widths the grid becomes one column. At 390 px every line wraps within the host, nothing overflows sideways, and nothing clips. Look: open grid rhythm with 1px rules between populated cells rather than a card around every item, square corners, no shadows, glow, blur, or rounded corners. Headings and copy inherit the page's font. Glyphs and small labels use the mono grid font. Only the first glyph uses the accent, as a single point of emphasis, and the accent is never text on paper. Any focusable element added by future data receives a 2px accent outline offset 2px on :focus-visible only, and any disabled native control is shown at 45% opacity. Set meta.wave to 8, meta.facets to ["static"], meta.palette to ["fg", "muted", "accent"], meta.host to "div", meta.stage to "flow", meta.wraps to "content", and omit meta.controlled and meta.interactions. Put the flow minimum in a :where() rule, never an inline style. Set meta.demo.children to

Built for the whole page.

Ten precise capabilities, without a framework.

. The core never hides, moves, rewrites, or draws over those children. It composes no cores. It is wrong if the glyphs become fetched icons, if the result reads as six empty bordered cards, or if prose is forced into mono. The 16384 byte sections budget includes shared runtime and any composed core. Expect about 4.5 KB gzipped with shared runtime because this composes none. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from createRng, createNoise, or hashSeed with the seed, though this design needs none, and looks finished and intentional on both the dark ground and the light one.
components.props: items (json, default six features: One source with glyph [1], React and HTML with glyph <>, Palette ready with glyph [#], Accessible by default with glyph {a}, Seeded motion with glyph ~~, and Small by contract with glyph KB, each with a short heading and one line of copy), columns (number, 1 to 4, default 3), gap (number, 0 to 3 rem, default 1.5), label (string, default "Features"). The inspector exposes items, columns, gap, and label.

components.title: Logo Wall
components.brief:
A page body section that follows the page's own heading and introduction with a wall of wordmarks supplied as strings. It never fetches, accepts, or creates images. The core builds a semantic list, and every wordmark remains readable text. The default frame contains twelve invented names of varied lengths in a four column wall, so every cell is occupied and neither half of the frame is accidentally empty. At 390 px it becomes two columns, permits long names to wrap, never overflows sideways, and never clips. Look: a quiet 1px outer rule and 1px separators, square corners, no shadows, glow, blur, or rounded corners. Wordmarks and the small partner count use the mono grid font with modest tracking. The page's heading and prose retain the page font. One accent box drawing plus sign sits before the first wordmark as the only accent mark. The accent never sets wordmark text on paper. Any focusable element added by future data gets a 2px accent outline offset 2px on :focus-visible only, and any disabled native control is shown at 45% opacity. components.title: FAQ List
components.brief:
A frequently asked questions section that follows the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Disclosure pattern. The page supplies the section heading and introduction as children. The core builds questions from JSON, [{ id, question, answer, disabled }]. Each question is a real button followed by its answer region. The button has aria-expanded equal to the answer's visibility and aria-controls pointing to that answer. Enter toggles the focused question. Space toggles the focused question. Tab and Shift+Tab use the browser's normal order to move between question buttons and surrounding page controls. Arrow keys have no special behavior because this is a list of independent disclosures, not the wave 6 accordion. Pointer click on the button toggles it, while clicking the answer or empty row space does nothing. Disabled questions use a disabled button, do not toggle, and remain visible at 45% opacity. It emits openChange only in response to input, with the ordered array of open question ids. It is controlled through open, where null means uncontrolled, with defaultOpen read once at mount. Set meta.controlled to { open: "openChange" }. The default frame shows five populated questions with the first answer open, so it is informative before input and contains no empty panel. Look: 1px rules between rows, square corners, no enclosing card, no shadows, glow, blur, or rounded corners. Questions and answers inherit the page's font. The + or − state glyph and row number use mono. Only the open row's state glyph uses the accent. Every button gets a 2px accent outline offset 2px on :focus-visible only. State changes are instant, with no load transition. Set meta.wave to 8, meta.facets to ["static", "interactive"], meta.palette to ["fg", "muted", "accent"], meta.host to "div", meta.stage to "flow", and meta.wraps to "content". Set meta.interactions to Tab, expect focus on the first question button, Enter, expect openChange with [], and expect aria-expanded false. Put the flow minimum in a :where() rule, not an inline style. Set meta.demo.children to

components.title: CTA Banner
components.brief:
A single call to action band for the middle or end of a page. The page supplies a heading and one paragraph as children, and the core adds exactly one real a[href] from label and href. Keyboard behavior comes from the platform. Tab moves focus to the link, Shift+Tab moves away, and Enter follows its href. Space scrolls the page and does not pretend the link is a button. Pointer click follows the href. The default frame has a concise heading, a complete sentence, and one action aligned in a populated horizontal band. At 390 px the action moves below the prose, remains full width only within the host, and neither overflows sideways nor clips. Look: 1px top and bottom rules, square corners, no card, no shadow, glow, blur, or rounded corners. The heading and paragraph inherit the page's font. A small mono label above them and the action's arrow glyph use mono. The action is the one accent use, filled in the accent with readable cssOn text, never accent colored text on paper. It has a 2px accent outline offset 2px on :focus-visible only. Hover is limited to a roughly 10% fg mix. If the action is disabled by an empty href, render nonfocusable explanatory text at 45% opacity rather than a fake link. components.title: Milestone Timeline
components.brief:
A narrative page section that follows the page's own heading and introduction with an ordered run of milestones from JSON, [{ date, title, copy }]. It differs from the shipped timeline-chart in purpose and structure. timeline-chart plots spans and point events against a measured time axis, offers SVG and glyph chart looks, and carries a hidden data table. milestone-timeline is an ordered content section with no quantitative scale, no axes, no duration bars, and no chart role. Each milestone is a populated list item with a mono ordinal and date, a prose heading, and a short description. The default frame contains five milestones. The current index marks the third milestone, and all five have content. On wide screens the list runs horizontally with connectors between items. In auto orientation at 390 px it becomes a vertical run, wraps every label, never overflows sideways, and never clips. Look: 1px connector rules ending in box drawing junction glyphs, square corners, no cards, shadows, glow, blur, or rounded corners. Titles and descriptions inherit the page font. Dates, ordinals, and connector glyphs use mono. Only the current milestone's junction and ordinal use the accent. The accent is not used for prose text on paper. Any future focusable element gets a 2px accent outline offset 2px on :focus-visible only, and a disabled native control remains at 45% opacity. components.title: Footer Sitemap
components.brief:
A page footer section that keeps the page's own brand note and legal copy as children and adds grouped navigation from JSON, [{ heading, links: [{ label, href }] }]. The core builds a footer landmark containing a nav with an accessible label, a heading for each group, and real a[href] elements in semantic lists. Keyboard behavior is native. Tab and Shift+Tab move through links in document order, Enter follows the focused href, and Space scrolls rather than simulating a button. Pointer click follows the href. The default frame contains four groups with four links each, plus complete brand and legal child copy, so there are no empty columns or bare framed cells. At 390 px groups become two columns and then one when needed. Long labels wrap, the focus outline remains visible, and nothing overflows sideways or clips. Look: a 1px top rule and quiet row separators, square corners, no card around the footer, no shadows, glow, blur, or rounded corners. Group headings and link text inherit the page's font. The small sitemap label and copyright figure use mono. One accent box drawing corner marks the sitemap label. Link text stays fg or muted, never accent on paper. Links receive a 2px accent outline offset 2px on :focus-visible only and a roughly 10% fg tint on hover. A disabled destination is rendered as nonfocusable text at 45% opacity, never an anchor without a destination. components.title: Signup Row
components.brief:
An email capture row that keeps the page's own heading and explanation as children and adds a real form with a visible label, input type=email, and button type=submit. It never posts or calls the network. On input it emits valueChange with the current string. On submit it prevents navigation and emits submit with { email } only when the native email field is valid. It is controlled through value, where null means uncontrolled, with defaultValue read once at mount. Set meta.controlled to { value: "valueChange" }. Keyboard behavior comes from the platform. Tab focuses the email input, the next Tab focuses the submit button, Shift+Tab reverses that order, and Enter in the field or on the button submits valid input. Escape has no special behavior. Pointer click places the caret in the input or submits through the button. Disabled makes both controls disabled and keeps them visible at 45% opacity. The default frame contains complete heading and copy and a valid example address in the input, so the interaction can be judged and verified immediately. At 390 px label, input, and button stack, the focus outline remains visible, and nothing overflows sideways or clips. Look: one 1px rule around the joined input and action on wide screens, square corners, no shadow, glow, blur, or rounded corners. Heading, copy, label, input text, and button label inherit the page font. The small privacy note uses mono. The submit button is the single filled accent surface with readable cssOn text. The accent is never input text on paper. Both controls receive a 2px accent outline offset 2px on :focus-visible only. Hover is limited to a roughly 10% fg mix, and state changes are instant. components.title: Feature Compare
components.brief:
A page body section that follows the page's own heading and introduction with a comparison matrix from JSON. The core builds a real table element with a caption from label, column headers with scope=col, and feature headers with scope=row. Columns are [{ id, label }] and rows are [{ feature, values }], where each value is a boolean or short string. Boolean true and false render visible yes and no text for assistive technology plus aria-hidden glyph marks, so color never carries meaning. It differs from the shipped pricing section. pricing presents tier cards, prices, feature lists, calls to action, and an interactive billing radio group. feature-compare presents a dense semantic matrix for scanning support across columns, with no billing state, tier cards, price figures, or calls to action. The default frame compares Starter, Team, and Studio across six fully populated feature rows. At 390 px the real table remains in the DOM but CSS presents each feature row as a stacked labeled block with every column name repeated visibly. It does not require page level horizontal scrolling, overflow sideways, or clip any value. Look: 1px row and column hairlines, square corners, no rounded panels, shadows, glow, or blur. The page heading and introduction inherit the page font. Table headers, short values, and yes or no glyphs use mono. Only the highlighted column's top rule uses the accent. The accent never carries table text on paper. Any future focusable node receives a 2px accent outline offset 2px on :focus-visible only, and disabled native controls remain at 45% opacity.
